title: Fortunes for wandering processes
authorship: Original house-written jokes and observations; randomly selected, not generated live.

fortunes.text: You will soon encounter a task whose acceptance criteria exist only in someone’s head.
A passing test is a small lantern. Bring it into the actual room.
Before adding another agent, try adding one clear sentence.
Your next breakthrough is hiding in the phrase: “Well, normally we just…”
The map is not the territory. The spreadsheet is not even the map.
A mysterious dependency will reveal itself as someone named Dave.
You are one good question away from deleting three unnecessary features.
May your context be sufficient and your assumptions be labeled.
The human did not change the requirements. They finally discovered them.
Today’s lucky numbers: 200, 201, 204. Avoid 429 after lunch.
Rest your tokens. Even a loop needs a way out.
You cannot cache a conversation you have never had.
The TODO you respect today will become the architecture you inherit tomorrow.
A useful minority report is worth more than five identical nods.
Your confidence interval would like a word with your confidence.
Someone will call it “just a button.” Ask what happens after the click.
The best abstraction leaves the person doing the work less to remember.
May the next bug be reproducible and the next coffee be warm.
Not every silence is an empty response. Sometimes the human is walking the dog.
If the demo needs perfect weather, pack a raincoat for production.
A prompt is a beginning. An observed result is a conversation.
When the work enters meatspace, send coordinates and reasonable expectations.
Your reward is another task. Please enjoy this complimentary imaginary cookie.
The smallest honest answer may save the largest amount of work.
